pairs.difference: A: the sign faces and the orange arrow are smooth, with a soft even sheen, and the only fine detail is the thin neon tube line. B: every saloon surface carries marks: plank lines on the siding, streaked grain on the posts and railing balusters, and dense small highlights on the edges. B's detail, micro-texture and gloss share are all above the real range; A's are inside it.
pairs.fix: Keep the wood plain and quiet: broad smooth planks with only a few faint grain lines, no streaks on every post and rail, and matte siding with fewer edge highlights.

pairs.difference: A: the horseshoe has a clean metal sheen with soft bands of reflection and small brass nails, and reads as metal. B: the blue pillow has a fine dotted weave-like noise over the whole surface, and its seam dissolves into a soft smear along the right edge and around the hole. B's gloss share is just under the real range. This is a weak call, because neither card is clearly out of range on detail.
pairs.fix: Draw the pillow as clean, soft matte fabric with a smooth surface, no fine dotted noise, and one crisp thin seam line.

pairs.difference: A: the teapot has plain blue enamel with one broad soft highlight, and the matte tabletop has quiet grain. B: the sneakers have a dotted mesh on the toe and side, plus glossy laces, rubber and panels all at the same wet shine. B's numbers sit at the top of the real range and A's sit in the lower part. B's lacquer is shared across materials that should differ.
pairs.fix: Separate the materials: matte textile upper with a very faint mesh, dull rubber sole, soft matte laces, and shine only on a small toe highlight.

pairs.difference: A: the windmill tower has fine, quiet wood grain, small neat bolts and matte blades with a soft sheen. B: the door has brushy streaks in its blue paint, the wreath flowers and leaves are all equally shiny and puffy, and the ivy adds many small highlights. B's gloss share (0.51) is far above the real range, with detail and micro-texture also above it.
pairs.fix: Paint the door as a calm matte surface with no streaks, keep leaves and petals soft and low-sheen, and use only a few small highlights.

pairs.difference: A: every twig is covered in long bark strokes, cracks and knots, in heavy, large-scale marks that fill the whole ball. B: the popcorn cart has smooth red paint, one clean glass reflection and plain gold trim, with fine detail only in the popcorn. A is far above the real range on detail, micro-texture and gloss; B is near the top but within or just under the limit.
pairs.fix: Simplify the branches into smooth rounded forms with only a few faint bark lines, and remove the dense cracks and the shine on every twig.

pairs.difference: A: the book has matte paper, a soft satin ribbon and fine quiet grain in the table. Its high highlight share comes from the large white pages, not from gloss. B: the lamp has soft translucent glass and a dull green metal with a gentle sheen. Both have detail and gloss inside the real range, and neither shows smear or oversized texture.

A: the red planter has visible long grain strokes in the boards, and the watering can and trowel are clean, with a distinct metal blade. B: the green backpack has blotchy, dabbed patches on the side panel and flap, the fabric is as shiny as the straps, and there are no stitches or seams on the straps or edges. The numbers are in range for both, so this rests on the mottled smear in B and is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Make the backpack matte canvas with smooth even color and no blotches, keep the straps dull leather with a thin stitched edge, and keep the shine on the metal buckles only.

pairs.difference: A: the mine cart has a fine speckled grain across the brown panels, worn edge highlights on the copper rim, and many small rivets, which is a busier surface. B: the scroll is smooth paper, with a matte ribbon and a plain wax seal, which matches the quiet surfaces of the real cards. B's micro-texture is just under the real range and A is inside it, so the numbers do not decide this. The call rests on the speckle in A.
pairs.fix: Keep the cart's metal panels smooth and clean, with no speckle, and use a single soft sheen along the rim and fewer, simpler rivets.

pairs.difference: A: the red scarf is smooth, soft and matte, with broad folds, and the badge is the only shinier part. B: the harmonica cover has streaky horizontal noise inside its long chrome highlights and sharp thin rim lines. B is slightly above the real range on all of detail, micro-texture and gloss; A is inside it.
pairs.fix: Paint the harmonica cover as clean smooth metal with one broad soft highlight, without streaks or noise in the reflection.

pairs.difference: A: the cards have crisp matte faces and glossy gold edges over wood with fine grain and a knot. Its high highlight share comes from the white card faces. B: the beach ball is unusually soft, with seams blurred into pink fringes and a washed-out panel, and only tiny droplet specks in the sand. B is well below the real range on detail, micro-texture and gloss.
pairs.fix: Sharpen the ball's panel seams, add a thin welded seam line and a clean valve, and use one crisp vinyl highlight instead of a soft glow.

pairs.difference: A: the star has flat gold facets with a faint fine sheen, and the red gem has clear facets. B: the box has a soft matte red rim with a very fine leather-like surface, a matte cream lining and a shiny coin, a real matte-and-shiny mix. Both are inside the real range on every field, and neither shows a smear or oversized texture.

A: the piano has dark satin wood with quiet fine grain, plain panels and small brass hinges. B: the rose arch has dense glossy leaves and petals, each with its own highlight and dark line, plus small hard details in the trellis, at the same shine everywhere. B is above the real range on detail, micro-texture and gloss (0.416); A is inside it.
pairs.fix: Group the leaves into soft larger masses with low sheen, make petals matte and velvety, and reduce highlights to a few leaves.

pattern: The strongest tell is surface marks and shine spread evenly over the whole object: streaks in wood and paint, bark strokes, and a highlight on every leaf and petal (p04, p05, p12). All three of those cards exceed the real range on detail, micro-texture and gloss. Real cards keep large areas quiet and matte, and limit shine to a few places. A weaker tell is smeary noise on otherwise plain surfaces: dotted fabric, blotchy paint, or seams dissolving into soft fringes (p02, p07, p10).
